title.value: Building Robust Ensembles via Margin Boosting
title.justification: The title of the paper is explicitly mentioned at the beginning and in several other sections such as the abstract and the contribution section of the paper.
title.quote: Building Robust Ensembles via Margin Boosting

analysis.description: This paper addresses the problem of adversarial robustness of neural networks by proposing a margin-boosting framework that constructs robust ensembles of classifiers. It introduces a new margin-maximizing cross-entropy (MCE) loss and a computationally efficient algorithm, MRBOOST, for learning such ensembles. The study shows that the proposed approach outperforms existing ensemble techniques and large end-to-end trained models on benchmark datasets.

type.justification: The paper involves extensive empirical evaluation on benchmark datasets to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm (MRBOOST) and the margin-maximizing cross-entropy (MCE) loss in improving adversarial robustness.
type.quote: Through extensive empirical evaluation on benchmark datasets, we show that our algorithm not only outperforms existing ensembling techniques, but also large models trained in an end-to-end fashion.

name.justification: The paper is concerned with constructing neural network ensembles that are robust to adversarial attacks, addressing their vulnerability to adversarial perturbations.
name.quote: In the context of adversarial robustness, a single model does not usually have enough power to defend against all possible adversarial attacks, and as a result, has sub-optimal robustness.

name.justification: The paper discusses constructing ensembles of neural networks to improve adversarial robustness, leveraging multiple base classifiers.
name.quote: Consequently, an emerging line of work has focused on learning an ensemble of neural networks to defend against adversarial attacks.

name.justification: The paper employs a boosting strategy, specifically margin-boosting, to create robust classifiers.
name.quote: We view this problem from the perspective of margin-boosting and develop an algorithm for learning an ensemble with maximum margin.

name.justification: MRBOOST.NN is a model that was derived from the margin-boosting framework and is implemented in the study.
name.quote: We derive a computationally efficient algorithm (MRBOOST.NN) from our margin-boosting framework.

is_contributed.justification: The paper presents MRBOOST.NN as a novel contribution aimed at constructing robust ensembles for adversarial defense.
is_contributed.quote: We derive a computationally efficient algorithm (MRBOOST.NN) from our margin-boosting framework.

is_executed.justification: The model was empirically evaluated using benchmark datasets, which implies that it was executed.
is_executed.quote: Through extensive empirical evaluation on benchmark datasets, we show that our algorithm not only outperforms existing ensembling techniques, but also large models trained in an end-to-end fashion.

is_compared.justification: MRBOOST.NN is compared to existing ensembling techniques and large end-to-end trained models to show its effectiveness.
is_compared.quote: Through extensive empirical evaluation on benchmark datasets, we show that our algorithm not only outperforms existing ensembling techniques, but also large models trained in an end-to-end fashion.

referenced_paper_title.justification: The paper does not cite another paper specifically for MRBOOST.NN, as it is introduced in this paper itself.

name.justification: CIFAR-10 is used as a benchmark dataset to evaluate the robustness and performance of the model and techniques proposed in the paper.
name.quote: We use CIFAR-10 dataset and use a nine-layer convolutional neural network as the base classifier.

referenced_paper_title.value: Learning Multiple Layers of Features from Tiny Images
referenced_paper_title.justification: The CIFAR-10 dataset is often attributed to this paper by Alex Krizhevsky, which is one of the original papers describing the dataset.
referenced_paper_title.quote: A. Krizhevsky, Learning Multiple Layers of Features from Tiny Images, University of Toronto.

name.justification: SVHN is used as a dataset in the experimental evaluation of the proposed techniques in the paper.
name.quote: We consider three datasets: SVHN, CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100.
